title: Next-generation AI for acoustic neuromas: From imaging to informed treatment decisions
summary: Vestibular schwannomas (VS), also known as acoustic neuromas, account for approximately 8–10% of all brain tumors and about 90% of tumors in a specific brain region called the cerebellopontine angle. While these tumors are benign, they can significantly impair patients' quality of life and require early detection and careful treatment. Detection is extremely difficult due to nonspecific and insidious symptoms, often leading to misdiagnosis as age-related hearing loss or middle ear infections. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is highly reliable, but manual evaluation remains time-consuming and dependent on the radiologist's experience. Training artificial intelligence (AI) on existing MRI images aims to improve detection and reduce the time required. With a reliable and well-trained AI capable of distinguishing between normal and abnormal brain structures, early detection could be achieved, and evaluation could become independent of the radiologist's experience, resulting in consistent assessments across different clinics.

interventions.name: AI-supported retrospective analysis of all patients with vestibular schwannomas (VS), also known as acoustic neuromas, in the period from 2013-2025.
